title: The Dream Salt Below

features.name: the salt bloom
features.desc-on-touch: Salt crystals have grown upward in geometric patterns, each one a tiny memory the ocean left behind when it learned to be still. You touch one and taste bitterness and sleep.

features.name: the salinity boundary
features.desc-on-touch: Here the ground transitions from dried to crystallizing. The archive's own knowing bleeds into the salt layer; the border between archive and dreaming is measured in parts per thousand.

features.name: the tide mark memory
features.desc-on-touch: A line of dark sand curves across the brighter salt. It marks where the last tide learned it would not return. The archive has filed this line as a sentence.

features.name: the evaporation tower
features.desc-on-touch: A structure built from the compressed memory of water that chose to become air and then became salt and then chose again to become land.

features.name: the sleeping mineral pool
features.desc-on-touch: Beneath the salt, the ground holds water that has stopped moving. It dreams the dreams of mineral sediment—slow comparisons, dissolution without haste.

inscription: this deep, salt knows it is both ocean and desert, both knowing and dream

reverie.title: REVERIE — salt lagoon at the stopping tide
narr: You both stand in the shallows where the water
has decided not to leave. She points at the salt
blooming on the rocks. "The ocean keeps teaching
itself," she says. You feel the ground shift under
your feet—not sinking, but becoming something else.
The corruption began here, you think. Or here it became beautiful.

exits.label: back up to the lagoon where tides still answer
deeper still, where the salt has learned to root
toward the edge where ocean gives up its shape
